agentSettings.defaultLanguageHint: A caller's _meta.language still wins; this is only the default. Empty = follow the input's language, then fall back to English.
agentSettings.needSaveLanguage: Save the agent first to configure its default reply language.
agentSettings.needSaveSkills: Save the agent first to configure skill bindings.
agentSettings.needSaveDiscovery: Save the agent first to configure skill discovery.
agentSettings.needSaveSupervisor: Save the agent first to grant super privileges.
agentSettings.skillsHint: Only bound skills are written into the prompt (name and description only; the agent reads the body on demand). This is the same data as Skill → Visibility: a private skill is visible only to its owning agent, and is listed here for reference only.
agentSettings.skillDiscoveryHint: When on, the agent can discover tenant-wide shared skills via list_skills and read them on demand (not written into the prompt); when off, only its own private skills and the skills bound to it are visible.
agentSettings.supervisorHint: Same level as the built-in super agent: can create, modify and delete other agents and skills, write files across domains, holds all built-in tools by default, and every entry point (including calls from other agents or flows) reads the draft. A tenant can grant it to multiple agents. The last supervisor cannot be revoked (otherwise nobody could grant it back).
agentSettings.supervisorGrantHint: Granting auto-completes the starter kit: replaces the default single tools under “Required” with the core tool groups (including agent-admin), turns on “Unrestricted tools” and “Allow discovering unbound skills”, and binds the agent-authoring / skill-authoring / custom-tool-authoring skills. Revoking does not roll these back (they stay, but the admin tools no longer execute).
agentSettings.supervisorCallableTip: A supervisor can be called; when invoked it still has the full admin surface (always reads the draft)
agentSettings.callDefaultTip: If not configured, nobody can call it by default
agentSettings.needSaveGrants: Save the agent first to configure tool grants. Without grants, supervisors (the built-in one and any granted later) hold all built-in tools by default; other agents bind no tools by default.
agentSettings.grantToolsHintPre: This is a supervisor: its tools come from
agentSettings.grantToolsHintMid: as any other agent (the built-in super agent and granted ones share one path, no special channel). The resident set = the six
agentSettings.grantToolsHintPost: groups under “Required” below (19 tools). browser plus skill-admin / tool-grant / custom-tool are not resident — their schemas are only granted while the matching skill is bound and are taken back on unbind. Deleting a core group permanently removes a whole capability class and asks for a second confirmation.
agentSettings.unrestrictedOnHint: On: whatever tool a skill says it needs is granted directly, no need to add it under “Allowed”; entries under “Denied” are still subtracted.
agentSettings.unrestrictedOffHint: Off: a tool a skill says it needs must be approved under “Allowed” first — this stops an agent from writing a skill that grants itself new powers.
agentSettings.noSkillToolDeps: No skill currently declares tool dependencies, so this switch makes no difference for now.
agentSettings.noGrantsSupervisorPre: No grants configured — a supervisor falls back to the “all open by default”
agentSettings.noGrantsSupervisorMid: branch (nothing is lost, but the grant table is no longer the source of truth). The built-in super agent runs
agentSettings.noGrantsSupervisorPost: to fill the core set; add them manually here for a newly created supervisor.
agentSettings.noGrantsPlainPost: by default and only works after you add grants.
agentSettings.summarySupervisor: supervisor: built-in tools are always available{unrestricted}, {n} tools in effect
agentSettings.summaryNoGrants: No grants: no tools are bound at runtime
agentSettings.previewNoGrantsMid: and is not a supervisor — at runtime it
agentSettings.previewNoGrantsPost: . Go back to the config and add grants.
agentSettings.previewDegraded: · allow grants not in effect: no injected skill declares tool dependencies
agentSettings.previewBaselineStrong: built-in tools are the fixed baseline
agentSettings.previewBaselinePost: , always available; grants only answer “what extra is given” (individual tools can still be explicitly removed under “Denied”).
agentSettings.previewExternalWarn: Entries marked “not executed” are external tools (MCP / RPC / local endpoint): the grant is in effect, but there is no invocation channel at runtime yet, so they are not bound to the model for now.
agentSettings.pickerSaveHint: Changes take effect after “Save” back in the config
agentSettings.skillToggleHint: Click an item to bind / unbind
agentSettings.agentToggleHint: Click an item to grant / revoke
agentSettings.mainCoreTitle: Resident group of the super agent: removing it loses this whole capability class for the super agent
agentSettings.unreleasedTip: No official version released yet: formal calls (MCP / RPC / endpoint / flow) will fail; only the editor's debug run works
agentSettings.catalogLoadFailed: Failed to load the tool catalog
agentSettings.grantsSavedPlatformBlocked: Tool grants saved; {n} item(s) are temporarily unavailable because the platform has not enabled or has disabled them
agentSettings.presetMissing: No built-in tool groups found, please retry later
agentSettings.supervisorGranted: Super privileges granted: core tool groups (including agent-admin) imported, unrestricted tools and skill discovery enabled, three authoring skills bound
agentSettings.supervisorRevoked: Super privileges revoked (tool grants and skill bindings are kept; admin tools no longer execute)
agentSettings.confirmRevokeCoreBody: “{name}” is a resident group of the super agent: removing it makes the super agent lose this whole capability class (takes effect on save, with no error). Revoke it?
